newsitem.title: CANADA: Lehman raises Bre-X price target.
newsitem.headline: Lehman raises Bre-X price target.

text.p: Lehman Brothers in New York raised its stock price target for Bre-X Minerals Ltd to US$22 from US$19 on Monday, market sources said.
The brokerage continued to recommend the stock as a buy, the sources added.

Bre-X was down 3/4 to 17-5/8 on Nasdaq on Monday and fell 0.85 to 23.55 in early trading today in Toronto. Lehman's price target hit the market after details of a letter from the Indonesian government to Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp were made public.
The letter from Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana gave the companies one month to settle with their local partners in the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia.
A letter, a copy of which was obtained on Monday by Reuters in Jakarta, was a reply to a joint submission from Bre-X and Barrick to develop Busang.

It said if Bre-X and Barrick failed to meet the deadline, all discussions between them and the government would be canceled. The government would then have full right to manage the richest parts of the Busang deposit, Busang II and III.
Investors appeared discouraged by the letter, interpreting it to mean Bre-X could lose its hold on Busang if the company did not clear up its complicated disputes with local partners.

"I'm quite encouraged," said Michael Fowler of Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion in Toronto. "I think what it suggests is that if Barrick and Bre-X don't make a deal, then the government of Indonesia would entertain other proposals."
Placer Dome Inc has asked the Indonesian government if it can merge with Bre-X to run Busang.
If Bre-X and Barrick could not work out the details of their deal, Indonesia might be prompted to examine Placer Dome's proposal or other methods of bringing Busang into operation, analysts said.
They said the ministry letter clearly showed that the Indonesian government, and not Bre-X, controlled the fate of Busang.
But international pressure on Jakarta to allow the bidding for Busang to unfold openly and fairly would probably stop the Indonesian government from taking the deposit away from Bre-X, analysts said.
"It's a possibility, but it's unlikely," said John Ing with Maison Placements in Toronto.
"Indonesia can't afford to shaft Bre-X," said Fowler.
Barrick shares fell 0.60 by midday on Monday to 36.25 in Toronto and by 3/8 to 27-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange. Placer Dome fell 0.60 to 28.55 in Toronto and by 1/4 to 21-3/8 in New York.
